# Testing: {{context}}

How {{context}} proves that something works. The tiers are the module standard's
([docs/standards/module.md](../../../docs/standards/module.md), "Testing").

## Tiers and commands

| Tier | Where | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typecheck | the whole module | `pnpm --filter @module/{{context}} typecheck` |
| Unit and architecture | `modules/{{context}}/src/tests/unit/` | `pnpm --filter @module/{{context}} test:unit` |
| Contract (the in-memory and Postgres adapters behave alike) | `modules/{{context}}/src/tests/contract/` | runs inside the unit and integration tiers |
| Scenarios | `modules/{{context}}/features/` | `pnpm --filter @module/{{context}} test:scenarios` |
| Integration | `modules/{{context}}/src/tests/integration/` | `pnpm --filter @module/{{context}} test:integration` (needs `TEST_DATABASE_URL`) |
| Workspace architecture | `tooling/architecture/` | `pnpm --filter @tooling/architecture test:unit` |

## Before a change is done

- {{the coverage bar for this context, for example: every new rule has a unit test, every new
  promise a scenario, every new query an integration test}}.
- Every tier above passes.

## What counts as a regression

Never acceptable to make a suite pass:
- weakening an assertion;
- `.skip`;
- widening a matcher;
- raising a timeout to hide a race;
- deleting a scenario.

## Legitimate reasons a test changes

- The behaviour it pins was changed on purpose, with a recorded decision.
- {{others specific to this context}}

Anything else is a finding to report, not an obstacle to route around.
